brief:
Today, 31 October, is Legs B at the New York gym. Nothing new has been logged since Pull B on 29 October: no Legs B landed for 30 October. If you trained last night and the save has not synced yet, this review will read it tomorrow; if you did not, tonight is Legs B and every number below is the same one you were given yesterday, on purpose, because no new session means no new numbers. Meso 3 restarted on 28 October: build through 24 November, deload 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December. The show, 1 March, is 121 days away.

What the review rests on: Push A on 28 October (typed in from memory, incline 175 for 6, chest press 135 for 12, crossover 12.5 for 12s) and Pull B on 29 October, logged live set by set, 20 of 21 sets in 46 minutes: chest-supported dumbbell row 50 lb for 8 on all four sets; close-grip pulldown 112.5 for 10, then 127.5 for 9, 9; straight-arm pulldown 45 for 9, then 37.5 for 10, 10; dumbbell shrugs 80 for 15, three sets (the slot asks four); incline curl 25 for 10, 30 for 9; reverse curl 27.5, 32.5, 32.5 for 10; face pulls 27.5 for 15, 15. Those are the first New York numbers the app watched happen, and every Pull B lift builds on them.

No change to the program today, same as yesterday, and for the same reason: two nights into the block, the Pull B numbers are starting points, and four of tonight's Legs B lifts have never been trained in their slots. What is being watched, with dates: the fourth shrug set (if the next Pull B also stops at three, it comes off); the Push A triceps slot, done as dips on 28 October instead of the overhead extension (one more Push night as something else and it is swapped for a triceps lift this gym has); the Push A lateral-raise slot, done as dumbbells on 28 October (if the next Push A is dumbbells again, the slot becomes what you actually do); calves, decided on 2 November from tonight; the leg extension, decided on 6 November from the first New York Legs A; and the nine muscles that read over their ceilings only by half-credit from compound lifts, decided on 9 November after one full rotation here.

The real gap is still legs. Over the last four weeks your quads have averaged under 2 sets a week, against 13 in the plan, because the leg nights were the ones that dropped on the road; the last quad work of any kind was 14 October. Tonight fixes that, but it is week one: stop each set with two or three reps left, not at failure, and expect soreness tomorrow.

Tonight, Legs B, 20 sets, every number in pounds. Barbell RDL: 135 for 10, then 155 for 8, 8 (you did 185 for 8 on 17 September; this rebuilds toward it). Smith squat: 95 for 8, three sets. Leg press with feet low: 180 for 10, three sets. Leg curl: 110 for 10, three sets. Ab wheel from the knees: 8, two sets, stopping when your lower back starts to arch. Cable crunch: 55 for 10, three sets. Calf press on the leg press: 250 for 12, three sets. None of these machines has a New York number yet, so every weight is a starting point: if the first set is clearly too light or too heavy, change it and log what you actually used.

Still open, and it matters tonight: is this New York gym the one you trained at in August, before you noted a new gym on 2 September? The calendar calls New York "the home gym", but the log has two home-gym periods, August (close pulldown 127.5 for 10 on 25 August) and September (the same pulldown at 88 on 15 September). The September gym is ruled out on its own note, no smith machine, and you logged a smith incline on 28 October; so the question is August's gym or a third one. Your 29 October close pulldown (127.5), straight-arm pulldown (45) and face pulls (27.5) match August, as did the incline and reverse pec deck on 28 October. If it is the August gym, tonight's leg numbers are light: your 16 August Legs B was leg curl 142.5 for 12 on four sets, calf press 300 for 12, cable crunch 60 for 12, against tonight's 110, 250 and 55. Until you say so, the review starts below those and lets you add weight when a set is clearly easy.

Still missing: no bodyweight logged since 23 August (207 lb). A morning weigh-in this week would anchor the block.

block.why: Meso 3 restarted on 28 October at the New York gym (build to 24 November, deload 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December; the show is 121 days away). Nothing new has been logged since 29 October (no Legs B landed for 30 October), so this review repeats yesterday's and says so; the moment a Legs B log lands, every Legs B lift gets its first New York read. Two nights are in: Push A on 28 October, mostly typed in from memory within a minute and a half, and Pull B on 29 October, logged live set by set with about two minutes between sets, 20 of 21 sets (one shrug set short). The rotation skipped from Push A to Pull B, so Pull A, Legs A and Push B still have no New York night, and tonight is Legs B, the first leg night since Chennai on 14 October. That is the block's biggest gap: quads have averaged 1.6 sets a week over four weeks against 13 planned, hamstrings 5 against 15.5, calves 1.5 against 9. The program is not short of leg work; the leg nights are what did not happen. No change to the program today. Pull B's numbers are the first live-logged New York numbers and, apart from one straight-arm set at 45 for 9 that he corrected to 37.5, they sit inside their rep ranges (chest-supported row 50 for 8s, close pulldown 127.5 for 9s, shrugs 80 for 15s, three of four sets), so they are starting points to build on, not reasons to restructure; the Legs B lifts added on 13 October (smith squat) and 26 October (barbell RDL, feet-low press, ab wheel) are untrained until tonight; the only lift with a reason to look again is the fourth shrug set, which was skipped on its first night and is watched, not cut, on one night. The open dates: calves on 2 November (tonight's Legs B decides it), leg extension moved to 6 November because Legs A cannot come round before then without three days straight, the counting-rule mismatch behind nine muscles that read over their ceilings on 9 November. Pull B also matches August on several machines (close pulldown 127.5, straight-arm 45, face pulls 27.5), which adds to yesterday's question of whether this is the August gym; it is still not assumed. The next boundary is the deload on 25 November: sets drop to about 60% and loads by 20%, and the prep block is written at the assessment from what these four weeks log.

chest.why: Eighteen direct sets a rotation since the 29 October cut (incline 4, two chest presses 6, two crossovers 5, dips 3), at its ceiling of 18. 8.8 a week done over four weeks. The only New York chest night is Push A on 28 October, typed in from memory (incline 175 for 6, chest press 135 for 12, crossover 12.5 for 12s). No new chest data since the 28 October night, two reviews running; nothing changes before the first New York Push B.

front-delts.why: Eight direct sets (incline press 4, Push B shoulder press 4), inside the direct range of 4 to 10; the 15 on paper is those 8 plus half a set from each chest press, dip and crossover set, which is why it reads over the ceiling of 10 (dated in deferred[] to 9 November). The Push A shoulder press came off on 26 October and Push A on 28 October ran without it. The Push B press last moved at Chennai, 25 kg for 8 and 9 on 15 October; Push B has not run at New York. No new front-delt data since 28 October. Hold.

side-delts.why: Eight direct sets a rotation (Push A raise 3, Push B dumbbell raise 3, the Pull A cable raise 2 added on 26 October) plus half credit from the Push B press, 10 on paper, against a floor of 8 direct. 3.9 a week done over four weeks. At New York only the Push A slot has run, on 28 October, as dumbbell lateral raises, 12.5 lb for 12s, typed in from memory. The Pull A cable raise has still not run: Pull A was skipped for Pull B on 29 October. Watching, not changing, until the Pull A and Push B raises have a New York night each.

rear-delts.why: Ten direct sets (reverse pec deck 3 and 3, face pulls 2 and 2), inside the direct range of 6 to 12; the 15.5 on paper is half credit from every pulldown and row (dated in deferred[] to 9 November). New York so far: reverse pec deck 90 for 13, 12, 12 on 28 October, face pulls 27.5 for 15, 15 on 29 October, both logged live. Hold.

lats.why: Seventeen direct sets on paper (wide pulldown 3, seated row 4, chest-supported row 4, close pulldown 3, straight-arm 3), 18 with the rollout's half credit, at the ceiling of 18; 8.3 a week done over four weeks. First New York Pull B on 29 October was logged live, set by set: chest-supported row 50 lb for 8 on all four sets, close pulldown 112.5 for 10 then 127.5 for 9, 9, straight-arm pulldown 45 for 9 then 37.5 for 10, 10. 20 of 21 sets done. Every lat lift has a New York starting number now except the Pull A pair; hold the structure and build reps on these machines.

upper-back.why: Eight direct sets (seated row 4, chest-supported dumbbell row 4), the floor of the direct range 8 to 16; the 19.5 on paper is half credit from every pulldown, deadlift, hinge and rear-delt set, which is why it reads over the ceiling (dated in deferred[] to 9 November). The chest-supported row ran for the first time on 29 October: 50 lb a hand for 8, 8, 8, 8, all four sets, the bottom of its 8 to 10 range. Hold.

traps.why: Four direct shrug sets planned since 26 October, the direct floor of 4; the rest of the 9.5 on paper is half credit from the deadlift, face pulls and lateral raises. The first night of four sets, 29 October, ran three: 80 lb dumbbells for 15, 15, 15. 3.5 a week done over four weeks. One night is not a pattern; if the next Pull B also stops at three, the fourth set comes off rather than staying on paper.

lower-back.why: No direct slot: the 3.5 on paper is half credit from the deadlift (4) and the barbell RDL (3). Held without a direct lift on purpose: a heavy deadlift and a barbell RDL in the same week already load the lower back on every rep. Deadlift 235 for 5, 5, 5 at Vancouver on 23 October with no complaint logged.

biceps.why: Eleven direct sets (dumbbell curl 3, hammer 3, incline curl 2, reverse curl 3), inside the direct range of 8 to 14; the 18 on paper adds half a set from each pulldown and row (dated in deferred[] to 9 November). 29 October at New York: incline curl 25 for 10 then 30 for 9, the same 30 for 9 as Chennai on 13 October; reverse curl 27.5 then 32.5 for 10, 10. Hold.

triceps.why: Eleven direct sets on paper (overhead extension 3 and 3, reverse-grip pushdown 2, dips 3), inside the direct range of 8 to 14; the 19.5 on paper adds half a set from each press and the straight-arm pulldown, which is why it reads over the ceiling (dated in deferred[] to 9 November). On 28 October the Push A overhead extension slot was done as bodyweight dips, 8, 10, 12, so Push A had no triceps isolation, and Push B already has dips. No new triceps data since then. Watch: if the overhead slot is done as something else again at the next Push A, the review swaps it for a triceps lift the New York gym has.

forearms.why: Six direct sets (hammer and reverse curls), inside the direct range of 2 to 8; the 12 on paper adds half a set from the dumbbell curl, the shrugs, the pushdown and the RDL (dated in deferred[] to 9 November). Reverse curl at New York on 29 October: 27.5, 32.5, 32.5 for 10. Hold.

quads.why: Thirteen direct sets a rotation (Legs A press 3, split squat 2, leg extension 2; Legs B smith squat 3, feet-low press 3), inside 10 to 18. 1.6 a week done over four weeks, the lowest of any muscle: the last quad work was a smith squat in the leg-press slot at Chennai on 14 October, 17 days ago. The plan is not short of quad sets; the leg nights are what did not happen. Tonight is the first leg night at New York and the first Legs B since Singapore on 5 October. Hold.

hamstrings.why: Thirteen direct sets (deadlift 4, barbell RDL 3, two leg curls 6), inside 8 to 14; the 15.5 on paper adds half credit from the split squat and smith squat (dated in deferred[] to 9 November). 5 a week done over four weeks. Tonight is the first barbell RDL in its own slot and the first leg curl since Singapore on 5 October (120 for 10, 10, 11). Hold.

glutes.why: Twelve direct sets (deadlift 4, split squat 2, RDL 3, smith squat 3), inside 6 to 14; the 16 on paper adds half credit from two leg presses and the abductor (dated in deferred[] to 9 November). 4.4 a week done over four weeks, because leg nights were the ones dropped. Tonight's RDL and smith squat are the first of the block. Hold.

adductors.why: Two direct sets on Legs A, the floor of 2 to 6; the 7.5 on paper adds half credit from the leg presses, smith squat and split squat, which is why it reads over the ceiling. Not logged since 80 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October. Next Legs A.

abductors.why: Two planned, exactly the floor, all on Legs A. Last 60 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October; skipped at Chennai on 14 October. Next Legs A.

calves.why: Six direct sets a rotation (calf press on the leg press, 3 on Legs A and 3 on Legs B), exactly the floor of 6. 1.5 a week done over four weeks: no calf work since Singapore on 5 October (290 for 15, 12, then 270 for 14). Tonight's Legs B has the calf press. Dated in deferred[] to 2 November: if tonight logs it, the slot stays on both leg nights; if it cannot be done at New York, calves get a slot this gym has, not nothing.

leg-extension.why: Last done at Warsaw on 28 September (145, 150 for 12); skipped at Chennai on 14 October. The dossier calls it stalled, but that is two different machines. Deferred to 6 November, when Legs A comes round with a rest day between nights (it could land as early as 3 November if he trains four days straight, and the decision is made the morning after whichever night it is): if that night logs it, the slot stays; if the gym has none, it is swapped for a quad lift the gym has.

hip-adductor.why: Last 80 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October; 110 for 15 at Warsaw on 28 September on another machine. Next Legs A sets the New York number.

hip-abductor.why: Last 60 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October; 110 for 15 at Warsaw on 28 September on another machine. Next Legs A sets the New York number.

standing-calf-raise.why: This slot is the calf press on the leg press machine. Done as itself: 300 for 12, 12, 12 on 16 August (gym not recorded), 290 for 15, 12 then 270 for 14 at Singapore on 5 October. The 220 and 280 figures from 21, 24 and 28 September were a different movement, a standing calf raise done in this slot, and the 21 September note on this slot said the weights made no sense, so they are not used. cable-crunch.why: 55 for 12, 12, 12 at Singapore on 5 October; 55 then 60 for 12, 10, 10 at Chennai on 14 October, typed in the next day, so remembered. Tonight: 55 for 10, three sets, on a New York stack.

db-lateral-raise.why: 7.5 kg for 10s at Chennai on 12 October (16.5 lb); 7 kg for 15s at Warsaw on 30 September. The 28 October Push A raise slot was 12.5 lb dumbbells for 12s, remembered. Next Push B: 15 lb, chasing 15s.

cable-crossover-high-low.why: Cut on 29 October from 3 sets to 2 (chest at the ceiling, Push B the longest night). The last two times it was a different exercise or a different stack: 45 kg for 15s at Chennai on 12 October, a low-to-high crossover on 15 October. The first New York Push B sets the number.

reverse-grip-pushdown.why: 55 kg reverse grip for 11, 12 at Chennai on 12 October; a rope pushdown on 15 October. Different stacks. The first New York Push B sets the number.

chest-supported-db-row.why: First night, 29 October at New York, logged live: 50 lb a hand for 8, 8, 8, 8, the bottom of the 8 to 10 range on every set. Dumbbells read the same anywhere. Next Pull B: 50 lb again, chasing 9s; 10 on all four sets earns 55.

lat-pulldown-close.why: First New York night, 29 October, logged live: 112.5 for 10, then 127.5 for 9, 9. Chennai on 13 October was 115, 130, 130 for 8 on a different stack; 127.5 for 10 on 25 August (gym not recorded). Next Pull B: 112.5 for 10, then 127.5 chasing 10, 10.

straight-arm-pulldown.why: First New York night, 29 October, logged live: 45 for 9, then dropped to 37.5 for 10, 10. 45 was too heavy for the 10 to 12 range on this stack. Next Pull B: 37.5 for 12 on all three sets; three 12s earns 45 back.

db-shrug.why: 80 lb dumbbells for 15, 15, 15 on 29 October at New York, three of the four sets the slot now asks for. Same 80 for 15s as 3 September; dumbbells read the same anywhere, and 15 is mid-range of 12 to 20. Next Pull B: 80 lb for 16 on all four sets, one rep a set and the fourth set done. If the fourth set is skipped again it comes off (see traps).

incline-db-curl.why: 29 October at New York: 25 lb for 10, then 30 for 9. Chennai on 13 October was the same, 25 then 30 for 10, 9. Dumbbells read the same anywhere, so that is two nights at 30 for 9, which is inside the 8 to 10 range, not a stall yet. Next Pull B: 30 lb for 10, 10.

cable-reverse-curl.why: First New York number, 29 October, logged live: 27.5 for 10, then 32.5 for 10, 10. Every gym's stack read differently (Chennai 77 to 99, Singapore 36), so this is the starting point. Next Pull B: 32.5 for 12, three sets.

barbell-rdl.why: Never run in its own slot, but the free-bar movement has been logged in the old smith RDL slot: "Barbell" on 5 September, 135 for 8, 155 for 10, then 180 for 10, 10; and 135, 165, 185 for 8 on 17 September, logged with no note at the September home gym, which he wrote on 2 September has no smith machine, so that 185 for 8 was a free bar too (yesterday's review and the 26 October change entry called it a smith night; the log does not support that). After 17 September the slot ran on smith machines: 155 for 8, 8 at Warsaw on 24 September, 185 for 8 at Singapore on 5 October, and a smith bar does not compare to a free barbell. A barbell is a barbell, so 185 for 8 six weeks ago is the mark to rebuild toward. Tonight is the first free-bar RDL in six weeks and the first leg night in 17 days, in a week meant to stop two or three reps short: 135 for 10, then 155 for 8, 8, and 180 is the next target once three sets of 8 to 10 are logged.

smith-squat.why: Never run in its own slot; Legs B has not run since 5 October. The only smith squat was in the Legs A press slot at Chennai on 14 October, 45 kg for 5, 7, 8, on a smith bar that weighs something different at every gym. The New York gym has a smith machine (the incline ran on it 28 October). The Chennai number was done first in the session; tonight the squat comes after the RDL, so it opens a little under it: 95 for 8, three sets, as a starting point.

ab-wheel-rollout.why: In since 26 October in place of the hanging leg raise, untrained. Bodyweight, 8 from the knees on both sets tonight, stopping when the lower back starts to arch.

deferred.why: Triceps (19.5 against a ceiling of 14) and eight more muscles (front delts, rear delts, upper back, biceps, forearms, hamstrings, glutes, adductors) read over their weekly ceilings in the program check, every one only by half-credit from compound lifts. The targets were written for that weighted count, while the reviews have judged by direct sets. After one full rotation at New York, by 9 November, the targets get rewritten for one counting rule or the sets get cut to fit them, from what that rotation logs. Two of the six New York nights are in (Push A 28 October, Pull B 29 October).

No calf work since Singapore on 5 October. Tonight's Legs B carries the calf press on the leg press, the first chance at New York. On 2 November the slot stays if tonight logged it, or calves get a slot this gym has; it does not go without a replacement.

Last done at Warsaw on 28 September, skipped at Chennai on 14 October. It is only on Legs A, which has not run at New York; after tonight's Legs B the rotation runs Push A and Pull A before Legs A, so Legs A lands on 3 November at the earliest (four nights straight) and more likely 6 November with a rest day between nights. Dated 6 November: if a New York Legs A has logged it by then, the slot stays; if the gym has none, it is swapped that day for a quad lift the gym has; if the log lands earlier, the decision is made the morning after.

overrides.reason: Last free-bar RDL was 185 for 8 on 17 September, six weeks ago; since then only smith RDLs and 17 days without a leg night, so tonight rebuilds it from 135 and 155 with two to three reps left in the tank.
First smith squat in its own slot and on this gym's smith; 95 is a starting point, so if the first set is clearly light or heavy, change it a step and log what you used.
No leg press since Warsaw (190 for 8) on a different machine, and tonight it comes after the squat; 180 for 10 is the New York starting point.
Last real leg curl was 120 for 10 to 11 at Singapore on 5 October; one step under on a machine you have not logged.
First ab wheel night: from the knees, stop when the lower back starts to arch.
Singapore was 55 for 12s; a New York stack you have not logged, so 55 for 10 to start.
Calf press on the leg press: 300 for 12s in August and 290 at Singapore on other machines, so 250 for 12 is a starting point; change it if the first set says so.

findings.finding: The barbell RDL card said the last free-bar RDL was 180 for 10 on 5 September and that only smith RDLs ran since, naming 17 September (135, 165, 185 for 8) as a smith night; but 17 September was at the September home gym, which he noted on 2 September has no smith machine, and the row carries no as-note, so that 185 for 8 was a free bar. The 26 October program change entry repeats the same misreading.
findings.why: Lift note, override reason and brief now say the last free-bar RDL was 185 for 8 on 17 September, six weeks ago, and name 180 as the target once three sets of 8 to 10 are logged; the 135/155 opener stands as a week-one rebuild after 17 days without a leg night. The 26 October change entry in program.json is history and is not rewritten; its error is recorded here.
